content:
maria: Heads up — EU SCIM provisioning started failing right after the scheduled KMS alias rotation (~07:10 UTC). Multiple customers (acme, betacorp) saw 403s from our /provision endpoint. Logs show: `jwe: decrypt error: unsupported alg "RSA-OAEP-256"`

aj: Copy. Can you paste the log link and sample request id? @devops-bot did the alias swap complete cleanly?

devops-bot: Alias rotation completed at 07:09:58 UTC: `redwood-scim-eu -> redwood-scim-eu-v2`. KMS reports successful key version promotion. No KMS API errors in the rotation job. Audit: https://logs.internal/redwood/rotations/1718880700

sam: Noted. I'm seeing a coincident IAM change around 07:10:05 UTC where `infra-automation` removed binding `roles/scim_writer` from service account `service-scim-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.

maria: Hmm — if the SCIM worker lost its scim_writer binding then it would fail to call KMS decrypt even if the ciphertext and key are fine. That would surface as 403-ish decrypt errors. Is the audit entry trustworthy? paste: `projects/infra-automation/changes: removeBinding {member: serviceAccount:service-scim-sa, role: roles/scim_writer} @ 07:10:05`

nina: This looks like a double-fault: alias rotation + RBAC removal back-to-back. SCIM flow needs both the right key and the SA to have decrypt permission on that KMS key. If SA lost IAM on the key, decrypt calls return PERMISSION_DENIED which our decrypt wrapper surfaces as a JWE failure.

aj: Action plan: 1) restore IAM binding to service-scim-sa, 2) restart scim-worker in eu1, 3) requeue failed jobs. @oncall can you run the restore command?

oncall: Running now: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/scim/cryptoKeys/redwood-scim-eu --member=serviceAccount:service-scim-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` and re-applied `roles/scim_writer` on the SA. ETA ~2m.

devops-bot: Role binding restored at 07:22:14 UTC. Restarting scim-worker eu1-pool-3...

aj: After restart, decrypt calls show success and downstream provisioning resumed. Can we confirm customer backfills?

maria: Confirmed — acme backfill finished for 12 users, betacorp partial (20/22) requeued and processing. Creating incident ticket INC-2026-213 for postmortem.

sam: Root cause draft: automation job that ran the KMS alias rotation had an overlapping IAM cleanup job (bug in change window logic) which removed the service account binding. When combined with key promotion, SCIM service could not decrypt and failed open to 403/provision errors.

nina: Immediate mitigations: 1) Add a pre-rotation RBAC invariant check (fail rotation if SA lacks required bindings). 2) Lock IAM change window during key rotations. 3) Add an alert when critical SAs lose scim_writer or cloudkms decrypt role.

devsec-bot: Triage: checked logs and no unauthorized access observed. No tokens or PII exfiltrated. Severity: low (privileged operation caused outage). Recommended: add perf/audit rule and mark for policy review.

maria: Thanks — I'll write the postmortem and schedule a follow-up with infra automation owners. Next steps documented in INC-2026-213. :thumbsup:

aj: Also adding a runbook step: if you see `jwe: decrypt error` and it coincides with a rotation, check IAM bindings on service-scim-sa first before rolling back keys.

maria: Agreed. Closing thread, will ping when postmortem is published.
